title: DetourBench: Trajectory-Level Evaluation of Interactive Agents with Exact Minimum-Action Bounds
abstract: arXiv:2611.20844v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Benchmarks judge language-model agents mainly by whether they reach the correct final state, not by how they got there. Endpoint scoring cannot separate an agent that retrieved exactly the evidence a decision required from one that read most of the environment, nor an agent that never located the evidence from one that stopped a single action short. Settling this needs a reference cost, and authored solutions establish only that a task is solvable, not that no shorter route exists.   We present DetourBench, which constrains the environment until that minimum is computable. Each task is a finite, partially observable transition system with unit-cost accesses whose resources become globally addressable after discovery. Exhaustive search yields the full-information minimum action count $L_0$ with a replayable witness; from graph-recoverable terminal states it also yields exact residual work $R_T$, which separates an episode that stopped one

translated_title: DetourBench：基于精确最小动作界限的交互式智能体轨迹级评估
translated_abstract: 现有基准主要通过语言模型智能体是否达到正确的最终状态来评判，而非考察其如何到达该状态。端点评分无法区分恰好检索到决策所需证据的智能体与阅读了环境中大部分内容的智能体，也无法区分从未找到证据的智能体与仅差一步动作就停止的智能体。解决这一问题需要一个参考成本，而人工编写的解答只能证明任务是可解的，却无法证明不存在更短的路径。我们提出DetourBench，它对环境施加约束，使得该最小值可以被精确计算。每个任务都是一个有限的、部分可观测的转移系统，具有单位成本的访问操作，其资源在发现后变为全局可寻址。穷举搜索可得出完整信息下的最小动作数 $L_0$ 及可重放的见证；对于图可恢复的终止状态，它还能得出精确的剩余工作量 $R_T$，从而区分仅差一步就停止的回合……
tldr: DetourBench通过穷举搜索精确计算任务的最小动作数，实现了对交互式智能体轨迹效率（而非仅仅最终结果）的严格量化评估。
en_tdlr: DetourBench computes exact minimum-action bounds via exhaustive search, enabling rigorous trajectory-level evaluation of interactive agents' efficiency rather than merely their final outcomes.
